# /crav1-existing-to-specs

lane: cross-cutting | group: Start | starter: yes | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 3
purpose: Turn a system that already exists into specs; asks repos only or repos plus a bundle, and one spec or system notes plus one spec per feature; or rechecks existing specs against the repos.
use_when: The user names existing repos, with or without a bundle to match
reads: Repos plus a bundle: Reads the repos and the dump. Repos only: Reads the repos the user named, and `docs/architecture/left-out.md` when that file is there.
writes: Repos plus a bundle: Writes `docs/system/` in the destination the user picks (gaps only when it exists, including a missing glossary and new rows) and one `docs/specs/<slug>/spec.md` per confirmed slice, including not in the code, then index rows. When a dump file it quotes is an imported source, also writes `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`, following `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/sources.md`. That check may write the transfer data policy after a yes. Cursor: `.cursor/rules/crav1-transfer-data-policy.mdc`. Claude Code project: `.claude/rules/crav1-transfer-data-policy.md`. It never writes a secrets choice into that file. A mail is written as text, `mail.md`, and the original mail stays outside the repo. For a mail, it lists each embedded image, inline or attached. It recommends convert to text when the image is a diagram, a table, or text that can be reproduced exactly, and compress otherwise. It asks once before the source folder is written. Auto-accept applies to those recommendations only when the transfer data policy clearly covers them. A `repos.md` it writes includes a `Synced at` column and leaves that cell empty. It does not set or clear an existing cell. Repos only: Writes `docs/architecture/spec.md` when that file is missing, `docs/architecture/left-out.md` for guesses that stay left out, and the `docs/system/` notes `/crav1-explain-existing-system` reads when those notes are missing. Sets `Synced at` on each repo it read and touches only those repos. Recheck: writes only `## Code with no slice` in `docs/system/landscape.md` (lines still true stay, covered lines come off, new gaps added, `## Dismissed` kept) and `Synced at` in `repos.md` for a repo read whole. Writes nothing into any spec, and never an open question.
leaves alone: Repos plus a bundle: Leaves application code, `plan.md`, `work-item.md`, and the rest of an existing landscape alone. Does not commit. Repos only: Leaves application code and the next feature alone. On the pass that creates the architecture spec while system notes are already there, that cell is the only edit to those notes. Recheck: leaves every `spec.md`, Match status, plan, task, and application code alone; stale claims are reported, not fixed.
limits: Repos plus a bundle: a slice that is not in the code stays thin and is not planned here. A quoted note in `docs/notes/` gets its slug in `used_by` and a `Full source:` link; notes are never absorbed. Repos only: before writing, one question per section (each named repo, inferred guesses, links, left-out) and every item stays listed. A later re-read adds only what is new to the spec and notes, sets `Synced at` for repos it read without rewriting the rest of that row, and removes a left-out line when the code shows it or that section dismisses it. A guess stays out until that section accepts it. A link is written only when the code shows it.
flow:
- **`/crav1-existing-to-specs`** is a starter option.
- It opens with two questions: repos only, or repos plus a bundle to match; and one spec (the architecture spec), or system notes plus one spec per feature.
- the map confirm is one card.
- `yes (Recommended)` writes what was shown.
- Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer.
- the map confirm prints a findings table in that same reply before the card.
- The card names each slice and its recommendation.
- It does not say `table above`.
- The card is not asked without the table.
- Repos plus a bundle (was `/crav1-match-to-specs`): Existing repos plus a dump → where the spec files go, then `docs/system/` (including `glossary.md`) and one spec per confirmed slice (done, partial, or not in the code).
- Fills a missing `glossary.md` when the folder already exists.
- A meaning the source does not state is `to be researched`.
- Repos only (was `/crav1-repos-to-spec`): When the user names one or more repos and wants the architecture the code shows, **`/crav1-existing-to-specs`** reads those repos and writes one architecture spec the lanes can extend (`docs/architecture/spec.md`) when that file is missing.
- It writes the system notes under `docs/system/` when those notes are missing.
- When a real system note is already there, it leaves those notes except the `Synced at` line in `repos.md` of a repo it read, and writes the missing architecture spec and `docs/architecture/left-out.md`.
- When the architecture spec or those notes are already there, a later re-read adds only what is new and does not rewrite lines that are already there, except that `Synced at` line in `repos.md`, and removes a left-out line when the code shows it.
- A guess that stays left out is written to `docs/architecture/left-out.md`.
- It is not `/crav1-add-to-spec`.
- Repos only (was `/crav1-repos-to-spec`): The user names one or more repos.
- Reads those repos and writes `docs/architecture/spec.md` when that file is missing, and the `docs/system/` notes `/crav1-explain-existing-system` reads when those notes are missing.
- When a real system note is already there, leaves those notes except the `Synced at` line in `repos.md` of a repo it read, and writes the missing architecture spec and `docs/architecture/left-out.md`.
- A later re-read adds only what is new and does not rewrite those lines, except that `Synced at` line in `repos.md`, and removes a left-out line when the code shows it.
- A guess that stays left out is written to `docs/architecture/left-out.md`.
- Not `/crav1-add-to-spec`.

## Choice words
- question: What to read
  - `repos-only`: repos only
  - `repos-and-bundle`: repos plus a bundle
- question: What to write
  - `one-spec`: one spec (the architecture spec)
  - `spec-per-feature`: system notes plus one spec per feature
- question: Recheck existing specs
  - `recheck`: compare the repos with the specs that exist; report code with no spec and stale claims; refresh the landscape note
  - `repos-vs-specs`: the same as recheck
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Repos plus a bundle: Calls `/crav1-create-feature-branch` in that destination when it already has commits. Repos only: Calls `/crav1-create-feature-branch` when the destination already has commits.
you run next: /crav1-add-to-spec; /crav1-tighten-spec; /crav1-finalize-commit
first: `/crav1-existing-to-specs @repo-a/ @repo-b/ @notes/old-spec.md @tickets/ The repos are what exists. The dump is what to match. Do not write code. Ask where the specs go, then map, and stop.`
